issues.summary: The public records name hardware/software/solar/maintenance contributors and describe actual 2018–2020 monitoring, a kernel-upgrade power/uptime problem, configuration experiments, and continuation with a 30 W panel and 168 Wh battery. They consider static versus dynamic delivery, smaller batteries and nighttime availability against a geographically split readership. This supports a bounded attributed historical governance/necessity implementation judgment, stronger than a generic policy; representative reader testing and current execution are not established.

A bounded pass may credit the documented measurements, alternatives and reasoned configuration response without demanding internal records or inventing representative research. issues.summary: The service-specific methodology/evaluation supports public disclosure and a historical reduction direction with dated energy/uptime results. Reported 9.53 kWh server electricity and 18.10 kWh including solar-system losses refer to 3 December 2018–24 November 2019; 95.26% uptime uses a different 351-day period. The 0.021 Wh figure is per unique visitor, not per pageview or complete browsing lifecycle. Solar electricity removes neither manufacturing impacts nor client/network impacts; the publisher explicitly models embodied energy separately. A page labeled updated October 21, 2024 does not make its 2018–2020 measurements current.
issues.requestedChange: Credit service disclosure and scoped historical goals evidence while preserving each metric period, denominator and modeled-versus-measured boundary. Do not compare these historical values directly with current SWDM or client-only GreenFrame, present lifecycle-zero emissions, or treat the fivefold historical page-weight claim as a matched audit result. Hosting remains cantTell for independently corroborated current operations; do not set a green-hosting flag from self-report alone. Request current independent operational corroboration only if current hosting status is needed.
